notes: Fetched TJ Maxx's mobile nav-menu JSON feed (navMenuData.jsp, curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_2_ios, per prior access notes for SR71/c76) and walked all 3119 nodes of navigationHierarchy checking every displayName for Bestsellers-type signal words (bestseller, best sell, top sell, popular, favorite, pick, staff, editor, top rated, most loved, customer/shopper favorite, trending, hot, buzz, viral). No node under Home (or anywhere else) carries such a label. The only near-miss is 'trending now', which exists at top level and under new-arrivals/the-runway/clearance -- but it is an apparel styling theme (children: denim on denim, stylist spotlight, animal print, suede season, elevated essentials, etc.), not a popularity/bestseller ranking, and it has NO Home child anywhere in the tree, so it never even reaches the Home department. Also probed https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/search?Ntt=bestsellers (HTTP 404, same access route) and robots.txt (HTTP 200, no Claude-specific disallow rule) as corroborating checks. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers PLP exists for TJ Maxx generally or for its Home department specifically -- this is a real absence, not a search/access artifact, since the nav feed is the site's own complete taxonomy, not a fallible site-search box.
